The **2024 Indian Premier League**, also known as **IPL 17** and branded as **TATA IPL 2024** was the 17th edition of the [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League"), a professional [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") league. The tournament featured ten teams competing in 74 matches from 22 March to 26 May across 13 venues.

The defending champions [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") were eliminated in the league stage. In the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indian_Premier_League_final "2024 Indian Premier League final"), [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") defeated [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") by 8 wickets to win their third IPL title. [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") of [Royal Challengers Bengaluru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bengaluru "Royal Challengers Bengaluru") scored the most runs (741), while [Harshal Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshal_Patel "Harshal Patel") of [Punjab Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Kings "Punjab Kings") took the most wickets (24). [Sunil Narine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Narine "Sunil Narine") of Kolkata was named as the most valuable player of the tournament.

## Background

The [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") is a professional [Twenty20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty20 "Twenty20") (T20) [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") league held in India, organised by the [Board of Control for Cricket in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Control_for_Cricket_in_India "Board of Control for Cricket in India") (BCCI). It is held annually since the [first edition in 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Indian_Premier_League "2008 Indian Premier League").[[1]](#cite_note-1) [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") were the defending champions, having won their fifth title in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Indian_Premier_League "2023 Indian Premier League") after beating [Gujarat Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Titans "Gujarat Titans") in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Indian_Premier_League_final "2023 Indian Premier League final").[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)

### Format

The format returned to the same as 2022, unlike 2023, with the group order being re-shuffled. Each team played twice against the teams in their group and the team in the same row in the other group, and once against the remaining four teams in the other group.[[4]](#cite_note-format-4)[[5]](#cite_note-groups-5) After the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tournament#Group_stage "Tournament"), the top four teams based on aggregate points qualified for the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Page_playoff_system "Page playoff system"). In this stage, the top two teams competed with each other (in a match titled "[Qualifier 1](#Qualifier_1)"), as did the remaining two teams (in a match titled "[Eliminator](#Eliminator)"). While the winner of Qualifier 1 directly qualified for the final match, the losing team had another chance to qualify for the final match by competing against the winning team of the Eliminator match (in a match titled "[Qualifier 2](#Qualifier_2)"). The winner of this subsequent Qualifier 2 match advanced to the final match.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

#### Rule changes

Bowlers could now bowl two [bouncers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bouncer_(cricket) "Bouncer (cricket)") per over, as trialled in India's domestic T20 tournament, the [2023–24 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–24_Syed_Mushtaq_Ali_Trophy "2023–24 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy").[[7]](#cite_note-7)

### Schedule

There was a possibility of the tournament being held abroad due to a possibility of inadequate security, as a result of a clash with [Lok Sabha Election 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indian_general_election "2024 Indian general election"). On 14 February 2024, the chairman of the Indian Premier League announced that the tournament would take place in India and that the schedule would be finalized after a discussion with the [Indian government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") and other agencies, with the allocation of matches to states to depend on the election schedule to be released by the [Election Commission of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Election_Commission_of_India "Election Commission of India").[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) On 21 February, it was announced that the schedule would be announced in two halves as the dates of the elections has not been confirmed till then.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

A part of the schedule of the season's fixtures was announced on 22 February 2024 which included the schedule for the first 17 days, consisting of 21 matches.[[11]](#cite_note-11) The opening match of the tournament was to be played on 22 March at the [M. A. Chidambaram Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._A._Chidambaram_Stadium "M. A. Chidambaram Stadium") in [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai") between defending champions [Chennai Super Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Super_Kings "Chennai Super Kings") and the [Royal Challengers Bengaluru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Challengers_Bengaluru "Royal Challengers Bengaluru").[[12]](#cite_note-Sched-12) The remaining fixtures were announced on 25 March with the last group match to be played between [Rajasthan Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Royals "Rajasthan Royals") and [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") on 19 May at [ACA Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_Cricket_Association_Stadium,_Guwahati "Assam Cricket Association Stadium, Guwahati"), [Guwahati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guwahati "Guwahati").[[13]](#cite_note-13) It was announced that both Qualifier 1 and Eliminator would be played at the [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium"), [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") from 21 to 22 May, and that Qualifier 2 and final would be played in Chennai, with the venue hosting its third IPL final after [2011](https://en.

Cricket final

The **2024 Indian Premier League Final** was played on 26 May 2024 at the [M. A. Chidambaram Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._A._Chidambaram_Stadium "M. A. Chidambaram Stadium") in [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai").[[1]](#cite_note-1) [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kolkata_Knight_Riders_season "2024 Kolkata Knight Riders season") qualified for the finals after their win in [Qualifier 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indian_Premier_League#Qualifier_1 "2024 Indian Premier League").[[2]](#cite_note-2) They competed with [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sunrisers_Hyderabad_season "2024 Sunrisers Hyderabad season"), who qualified for the finals after their win in [Qualifier 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indian_Premier_League#Qualifier_2 "2024 Indian Premier League").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

After winning the toss, [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") elected to bat but only managed to score 113 runs in 18.3 overs. The [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") easily chased the target in 10.3 overs and won the match by eight wickets, thus winning their third IPL title.[[4]](#cite_note-4) KKR player [Mitchell Starc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitchell_Starc "Mitchell Starc") was named as the [player of the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_Match_awards_(cricket) "Player of the Match awards (cricket)") for taking 2 wickets and 2 catches.[[5]](#cite_note-5) [Sunil Narine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Narine "Sunil Narine") (KKR) was named as the player of the season for scoring 488 runs and taking 17 wickets throughout the tournament.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

## Background

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=2024_Indian_Premier_League_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

A part of the schedule of the season's fixtures was announced on 22 February 2024 which included the schedule for the first 17 days, consisting of 21 matches.[[7]](#cite_note-7) The remaining fixtures were announced on 25 March 2024.[[8]](#cite_note-8) It was announced that both Qualifier 1 and Eliminator would be played at the [Narendra Modi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium "Narendra Modi Stadium"), [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad") from 21 to 22 May, and that Qualifier 2 and final would be played in Chennai, with the venue hosting its third IPL final after [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Indian_Premier_League_final "2011 Indian Premier League final") and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Indian_Premier_League_final "2012 Indian Premier League final").[[9]](#cite_note-9) [Kolkata Knight Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Knight_Riders "Kolkata Knight Riders") and [Sunrisers Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrisers_Hyderabad "Sunrisers Hyderabad") qualified for the Final. Kolkata played the final for the fourth time, winning twice ([2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Indian_Premier_League "2012 Indian Premier League"), [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League "2014 Indian Premier League")) before and being runners-up in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Indian_Premier_League "2021 Indian Premier League"). Hyderabad played their third final, winning once in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_Premier_League "2016 Indian Premier League") and runners-up in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Indian_Premier_League "2018 Indian Premier League").[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11)

## Road to the final

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=2024_Indian_Premier_League_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Road to the final")]

Further information: [2024 Kolkata Knight Riders season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kolkata_Knight_Riders_season "2024 Kolkata Knight Riders season") and [2024 Sunrisers Hyderabad season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Sunrisers_Hyderabad_season "2024 Sunrisers Hyderabad season")

Kolkata Knight Riders had a successful league stage with only 3 losses against Chennai Super Kings, Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings. They also had 2 abandoned matches against Gujarat Titans and Rajasthan Royals. They won the rest 9 matches garnering a total of 20 points finishing atop the league table. They defeated Sunrisers Hyderabad in Qualifier 1 to gain their place in the Final.[[12]](#cite_note-:3-12)[[13]](#cite_note-:4-13)

Sunrisers Hyderabad finished second in the league table winning 8 games and losing 5 games to end with a total of 17 points. Their game against Gujarat Titans was abandoned. They lost the Qualifier 1 to Kolkata Knight Riders and had to defeat Rajasthan Royals in Qualifier 2 for a place in the Final.[[12]](#cite_note-:3-12)[[13]](#cite_note-:4-13)
